notes: Axia DESQ is sold as a two-piece system: a compact desktop control surface (6 faders, ~15.3x15.3x2.8in, no rack space) that links via a single proprietary 6-pin "latch-and-lock" CANBus/DC-power cable to a separate 1RU QOR.16 (or QOR.32) integrated console engine. All audio, network, GPIO, and AC power connectors physically live on the QOR.16 engine's rear panel, not on the DESQ surface itself — the DESQ-to-QOR link cable and the QOR's auxiliary/accessory-panel connector are proprietary system interconnects, not general-purpose signal/power ports, so they are omitted from the port list. Analog and AES/EBU audio I/O use RJ-45 jacks wired to Axia's StudioHub+ balanced-audio pinout, not standard Ethernet — grade is intentionally omitted on those. GPIO ports are opto-isolated DA-15 (2-row D-sub) connectors; the provided connector enum has no DA-15/DB-25 option, so they were mapped to the closest available id "vga" (a DB15 shell) purely as an approximation — physical pin layout does not match true VGA. Rack units omitted because the DESQ control surface itself is a desktop unit (the paired QOR.16 engine is 1RU, sold/shipped separately). Two DESQ surfaces (or one DESQ + one RAQ) can share a single QOR.16. Extracted from Axia's own "RAQ/DESQ Installation & User's Guide" (Rev 1.1.1, Jan 2019), Figure 1-2 QOR.16 rear-panel diagram, cross-checked against Telos Alliance's official DESQ product page.
